content:
**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected part**: Banana fruit bunch (fingers/hands)
- **Key features**:
  - The tips (blossom/distal ends) of numerous banana fingers show dark brown to black, shriveled, necrotic rot
  - The rot starts at the tip and progresses inward along the finger
  - The rotted tips look dry, sunken, and collapsed — resembling the ash end of a cigar
  - The rachis (central stalk of the bunch) shows brownish discoloration as well
  - The rest of the fingers remain green and apparently healthy

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Cigar End Rot**: Caused by fungi (*Verticillium theobromae* / *Trachysphaera fructigena*), this disease causes the distal (blossom) end of banana fingers to turn dark brown/black, dry, and shrivel — closely resembling the burnt end of a cigar. This precisely matches the image.
- **Anthracnose**: Causes sunken dark lesions on ripe/mature fruit surface, not specifically tip-confined necrosis.
- **Bunchy_Top / Banana_Bunchy_Top_Virus**: Leaf-based disease with narrow, streaked, crowded leaves — no fruit tip rot.
- **Cordana Leaf Spot / Sigatoka**: Leaf diseases only.
- **Panama Disease**: Internal vascular browning, leaf yellowing/wilt — not fruit tip necrosis.

The pattern of dark, dry, shriveled necrosis confined to the distal tips of the banana fingers is the hallmark sign of **Cigar End Rot**.
